programs.nl_rule:
The input is a large grid with a black (.) background containing exactly four small red (R) shapes, each fitting within a 3×3 bounding box. The four shapes are spatially distributed across the grid so that two appear in the upper portion and two in the lower portion, and within each vertical half, one is to the left and one is to the right. This gives four quadrant-based positions: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right. Each 3×3 shape is a distinct pattern of red and black cells.

1. Identify the four 3×3 red shapes in the input grid. Determine each shape's quadrant position (upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right) based on its relative location compared to the other shapes. 2. Extract each shape as a 3×3 subgrid of R and . cells. 3. Construct a 7×7 output grid by placing the four 3×3 shapes in a 2×2 arrangement: upper-left shape goes in rows 0-2, columns 0-2; upper-right shape goes in rows 0-2, columns 4-6; lower-left shape goes in rows 4-6, columns 0-2; lower-right shape goes in rows 4-6, columns 4-6. 4. Fill the separator row (row 3) entirely with black (.) and the separator column (column 3) entirely with black (.).

The output grid is always 7 columns wide and 7 rows tall. It consists of four 3×3 blocks arranged in a 2×2 layout, separated by a single-cell-wide black divider: column 3 is all black and row 3 is all black. The background color is black (.).
